minor.issue: The seeded 603 record is ALREADY status=reopened / failed_resolution=true / attempts=1 / resolved_at=null — it is not a 'RESOLVED + resident_confirmed' ticket as described in the QA brief. The reopen path still fires (Claude classifies the new message as returned_resolved), but if the AI ever classifies it 'same_open' the record would only bump contact_count and attempts would not increment. For a deterministic contest demo consider seeding 603 as resolved+confirmed and letting the demo submission perform the reopen.

impact() calls dashboard(user) internally, which loops interactions per issue for median FRT (N+1 queries). The Overview now fires /issues, /dashboard, /incidents/detect and /impact in parallel, so the FRT loop runs twice per dashboard load. Cheap at 21 issues, but O(n) queries on volume.
The public resident portal fires /api/auth/me on load and gets 401 twice per page load (visible as red console errors on the resident page). Harmless but noisy in a demo with the console open.

integration_issues.issue: The submission result card shows 'Answered from property documents' but never renders result.auto_response / answer_source, so a resident who asks 'What time does the pool close?' does not see the answer until they switch to My Requests. ResidentPortal.jsx submission-result block (lines ~152-176) has no auto_response branch, although the My Requests card (lines 276-281) does.

critical_code_review_comments: /api/impact re-invokes dashboard() (which does a per-issue interactions query for median FRT); extract the FRT computation or cache it so the Overview does not run that loop twice per load.

ImpactStrip returns null while impact is loading and on fetch error (load() only toasts), so a failing /api/impact silently removes the whole strip with no skeleton or error state — add a loading/error placeholder.
server.py is 1527 lines; /impact, /insights, /residents/thread and /approve-answer are appended after the document handlers. Split into routers before adding anything further.

Resolution Memory depends entirely on a single Claude JSON call (match_existing_issue); if the LLM is slow/unavailable it returns None and a duplicate ticket is created with no deterministic fallback (e.g. same-category + entity overlap within N days). This is the app's headline feature — a fallback matcher would de-risk the live demo.

rca_of_the_issue: No functional defects found in the two changes under test. /api/impact now computes conf_rate over status=='resolved' with the same expression as /dashboard, so the strip and the Confirmed Resolution card cannot diverge. Resolution Memory works because match_existing_issue() returns relationship='returned_resolved' with problem_persists=true for the 603 sink message, which drives the in-place reopen (no insert on the issues collection) — the only fragility is that this path is 100% LLM-dependent with no deterministic fallback.
